page: Amazon Web Services r8id.12xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.9 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates a 480 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector processing and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) for hardware-accelerated matrix operations.

System memory consists of 384 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Ephemeral storage is bundled directly onto the instance through 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while baseline network throughput is rated at 22 Gbps. In memory-intensive benchmarks, the architecture demonstrates strong throughput, reaching 3840.86 GB/sec on cached read operations and 192.31 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers. Redis key-value workloads achieve 85.77 million SET operations per second, supported by solid database operational metrics.

General compute benchmarks indicate consistent upper-quartile execution. PassMark CPU tests yield 69124.82 points, with Geekbench recording 2190.0 in single-core and 19680.0 in multi-core evaluation. While standard synthetic stress-ng compute tests rank within the middle tier, instruction extensions yield high performance in cryptographic processing, text processing, and decompression. Intel AMX capabilities also facilitate CPU-based LLM inference, delivering 333.34 tokens per second during small model text generation.

The integration of dense DDR5 memory, direct-attached high-speed NVMe storage, and modern Intel matrix execution units makes r8id.12xlarge an efficient platform for resource-heavy services. It is technically configured for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, low-latency relational database management systems, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance featuring an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz. It includes advanced hardware extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside a 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured with 384 GB of high-frequency DDR5, offering 8 GB of memory per core. Bundled storage delivers 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, paired with 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-quartile performance in memory read bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and Redis throughput at 85.77 million operations per second. CPU-bound matrix tasks and small model inference also benefit directly from integrated AMX accelerators. This hardware configuration delivers balanced resource density and performance for in-memory databases, real-time caching, enterprise data pipelines, and analytics workloads.
